title: A Count in Knots
author: a warlord's reckoner
pages:
Set down from the knot-cord, as near as it can be said in words.

River town: paid. Did not burn.
Hill town: paid short. Burned a little.

Mill town: gate shut. Burned.

The ring-nosed one says the soft folk always pay the second time.
The door stood open nine days and then it did not. We do not open the doors. We wait by them. Somebody up there always lights one.
